# A loop may start anywhere, stop at any integer expression that is the same on
# every evaluation, be written with <=, and count down to a bound. Every access is
# still at exactly index i, so no two iterations touch the same element and only
# the range of indexes changes. The rewritten loop runs forward over the same
# indexes, never touches an element outside them (Short stops one before the end
# of dst), and panics when the scalar loop would; only the state left behind by a
# panic differs, since the lengths are checked before anything is written.

# The scalar program is the reference behavior.
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want
cmp ops.go ops.go.guarded

# The simd build must behave identically.
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

// The loop starts after the first element.
func StartOne(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 1; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] * 2
	}
}

// The limit stops one short of len(dst): the last element must not be written.
func Short(dst, a, b []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}

func Inclusive(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 0; i <= len(dst)-2; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] - 1
	}
}

// Both ends are variables, so the loop may be empty or run past the data.
func Window(dst, a, b []float32, lo, hi int) {
	for i := lo; i < hi; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}

func Half(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst)/2; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] ^ 7
	}
}

// Counting down, from an expression and to a variable.
func Down(dst, a []int32, n, lo int) {
	for i := n - 1; i >= lo; i-- {
		dst[i] += a[i]
	}
}

func DownStrict(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := len(dst) - 2; i > 0; i-- {
		dst[i] = a[i] + 5
	}
}

// A copy that starts at an offset.
func CopyFrom(dst, src []int32, from int) {
	for i := from; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = src[i]
	}
}

// A reduction over the inside of a slice.
func SumInner(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := 1; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		s += a[i]
	}
	return s
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import (
	"simd"
	"unsafe"
)

// The loop starts after the first element.
func StartOne(dst, a []int32) {
	_vcInt32s0 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(2)
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 1, len(dst), 1, len(dst)) {
		for i := 1; i < len(dst); i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i] * 2
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst) > 1 {
			_ = a[len(dst)-1]
			for _i := 1; _i < len(dst); {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i:])
				_v1.Mul(_vcInt32s0).StorePart(dst[_i:])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// The limit stops one short of len(dst): the last element must not be written.
func Short(dst, a, b []int32) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 0, len(dst)-1, 0, len(dst)-1) || _loopvecOverlap(dst, b, 0, len(dst)-1, 0, len(dst)-1) {
		for i := 0; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst)-1 > 0 {
			_ = dst[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			_ = a[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			_ = b[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(dst)-1; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(b[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_v1.Add(_v2).StorePart(dst[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

func Inclusive(dst, a []int32) {
	_vcInt32s2 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(1)
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 0, len(dst)-1, 0, len(dst)-1) {
		for i := 0; i <= len(dst)-2; i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i] - 1
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst)-1 > 0 {
			_ = dst[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			_ = a[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(dst)-1; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_v1.Sub(_vcInt32s2).StorePart(dst[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Both ends are variables, so the loop may be empty or run past the data.
func Window(dst, a, b []float32, lo, hi int) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, lo, hi, lo, hi) || _loopvecOverlap(dst, b, lo, hi, lo, hi) {
		for i := lo; i < hi; i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
		}
	} else {
		if hi > lo {
			_ = dst[hi-1]
			_ = a[hi-1]
			_ = b[hi-1]
			for _i := lo; _i < hi; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(a[_i:hi])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(b[_i:hi])
				_v1.Add(_v2).StorePart(dst[_i:hi])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

func Half(dst, a []int32) {
	_vcInt32s4 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(7)
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 0, len(dst)/2, 0, len(dst)/2) {
		for i := 0; i < len(dst)/2; i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i] ^ 7
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst)/2 > 0 {
			_ = dst[(len(dst)/2)-1]
			_ = a[(len(dst)/2)-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(dst)/2; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i : len(dst)/2])
				_v1.Xor(_vcInt32s4).StorePart(dst[_i : len(dst)/2])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Counting down, from an expression and to a variable.
func Down(dst, a []int32, n, lo int) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, lo, n, lo, n) {
		for i := n - 1; i >= lo; i-- {
			dst[i] += a[i]
		}
	} else {
		if n > lo {
			_ = dst[n-1]
			_ = a[n-1]
			for _i := lo; _i < n; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(dst[_i:n])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i:n])
				_v1.Add(_v2).StorePart(dst[_i:n])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

func DownStrict(dst, a []int32) {
	_vcInt32s6 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(5)
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 1, len(dst)-1, 1, len(dst)-1) {
		for i := len(dst) - 2; i > 0; i-- {
			dst[i] = a[i] + 5
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst)-1 > 1 {
			_ = dst[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			_ = a[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			for _i := 1; _i < len(dst)-1; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_v1.Add(_vcInt32s6).StorePart(dst[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// A copy that starts at an offset.
func CopyFrom(dst, src []int32, from int) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, src, from, len(dst), from, len(dst)) {
		for i := from; i < len(dst); i++ {
			dst[i] = src[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst) > from {
			_ = src[len(dst)-1]
			copy(dst[from:], src[from:])
		}
	}
}

// A reduction over the inside of a slice.
func SumInner(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	if len(a)-1 > 1 {
		_ = a[(len(a)-1)-1]
		{
			_i := 1
			if (len(a)-1)-1 >= 64 {
				_a1 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(0)
				_lanes := _a1.Len()
				for ; _i+_lanes <= len(a)-1; _i += _lanes {
					_v1 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i:])
					_a1 = _a1.Add(_v1)
				}
				var _buf1 [16]int32
				_a1.Store(_buf1[:])
				for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
					s = s + _x
				}
			}
			for i := _i; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
				s += a[i]
			}
		}
	}
	return s
}

func _loopvecOverlap[T any](a, b []T, window ...int) bool {
	aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi := 0, len(a), 0, len(b)
	if len(window) == 4 {
		aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi = window[0], window[1], window[2], window[3]
	}
	if aLo >= aHi || bLo >= bHi {
		return false
	}
	size := unsafe.Sizeof(a[0])
	aBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(a)))
	bBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)))
	aStart, aEnd := aBase+uintptr(aLo)*size, aBase+uintptr(aHi)*size
	bStart, bEnd := bBase+uintptr(bLo)*size, bBase+uintptr(bHi)*size
	return aStart < bEnd && bStart < aEnd
}
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/test"
)

var sizes = []int{0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17, 33, 64, 65, 100, 131}

func fill(n int, v int32) []int32 {
	s := make([]int32, n)
	for i := range s {
		s[i] = v
	}
	return s
}

func ramp(n int, scale int32) []int32 {
	s := make([]int32, n)
	for i := range s {
		s[i] = int32(i+1) * scale
	}
	return s
}

func sum(s []int32) (t int64) {
	for i, v := range s {
		t += int64(v) * int64(i+1)
	}
	return t
}

// try reports whether f panicked instead of what it did.
func try(f func()) (panicked bool) {
	defer func() { panicked = recover() != nil }()
	f()
	return false
}

func main() {
	for _, n := range sizes {
		a, b := ramp(n, 3), ramp(n, 5)

		d1, d2, d3, d4 := fill(n, -1), fill(n, -1), fill(n, -1), fill(n, -1)
		p1 := try(func() { test.StartOne(d1, a) })
		test.Short(d2, a, b)
		test.Inclusive(d3, a)
		test.Half(d4, a)
		fmt.Println(n, "A", p1, sum(d1), sum(d2), sum(d3), sum(d4))

		d5, d6, d7 := fill(n, 100), fill(n, 100), fill(n, -1)
		p5 := try(func() { test.Down(d5, a, n, 0) })
		p6 := try(func() { test.Down(d6, a, n-1, 1) })
		p7 := try(func() { test.DownStrict(d7, a) })
		fmt.Println(n, "B", p5, p6, p7, sum(d5), sum(d6), sum(d7))

		d8, d9 := fill(n, -1), fill(n, -1)
		p8 := try(func() { test.CopyFrom(d8, a, 2) })
		p9 := try(func() { test.CopyFrom(d9, a, 0) })
		fmt.Println(n, "C", p8, p9, sum(d8), sum(d9), test.SumInner(a))

		// A window: empty, inside, touching the end, and past it.
		f, g, h := make([]float32, n), make([]float32, n), make([]float32, n)
		for i := range f {
			f[i], g[i] = float32(i), float32(2*i)
		}
		for _, w := range [][2]int{{0, 0}, {n, 0}, {1, n}, {n / 2, n}, {0, n + 1}, {n, n}} {
			out := make([]float32, n)
			p := try(func() { test.Window(out, f, g, w[0], w[1]) })
			var t float32
			for i, v := range out {
				t += v * float32(i+1)
			}
			if p {
				// The rewritten loop checks the lengths first and panics before it
				// writes anything; the scalar loop has written what came before the
				// bad index. Only the panic is the same.
				t = 0
			}
			fmt.Println(n, "W", w, p, t)
		}
		_ = h
	}
}

-- ops.go.guarded --
//go:build !goexperiment.simd

package test

// The loop starts after the first element.
func StartOne(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 1; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] * 2
	}
}

// The limit stops one short of len(dst): the last element must not be written.
func Short(dst, a, b []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}

func Inclusive(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 0; i <= len(dst)-2; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] - 1
	}
}

// Both ends are variables, so the loop may be empty or run past the data.
func Window(dst, a, b []float32, lo, hi int) {
	for i := lo; i < hi; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}

func Half(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst)/2; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i] ^ 7
	}
}

// Counting down, from an expression and to a variable.
func Down(dst, a []int32, n, lo int) {
	for i := n - 1; i >= lo; i-- {
		dst[i] += a[i]
	}
}

func DownStrict(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := len(dst) - 2; i > 0; i-- {
		dst[i] = a[i] + 5
	}
}

// A copy that starts at an offset.
func CopyFrom(dst, src []int32, from int) {
	for i := from; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = src[i]
	}
}

// A reduction over the inside of a slice.
func SumInner(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := 1; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		s += a[i]
	}
	return s
}
